GeoQC Flow

Sharper Shape GroupGeospatial Data EngineerInternal production tooling

A Python CLI that automates quality control across multi-step FileGDB pipelines. It compares layers step by step, classifies geometry changes by severity, separates real attribute edits from system noise, and generates interactive HTML and DOCX reports from a single command.

Source code is not public. GeoQC Flow is internal tooling built for Sharper Shape production use, so the repository stays private. The implementation details below are described rather than linked for that reason. Happy to walk through the architecture in conversation.

Usage

# Activate environment and run
conda activate geoqcflow
geo-qc-flow run --pipeline-folder "C:\path\to\pipeline" --output "C:\path\to\reports"

Key capabilities

Auto-discovery
Detects numbered step folders and FileGDB files automatically. No hardcoded filenames: point it at a pipeline folder and run.
Smart feature matching
Auto-detects unique ID fields at 90% uniqueness or better, and falls back to index-based matching for layers without structured IDs.
Real change detection
Distinguishes genuine edits from system noise. Whitespace normalisation, null handling and case differences are filtered out before anything is flagged.
Smart remarks engine
A rule-based system generates alerts, warnings and notices flagging high-change layers, identical steps and derived layers.

Smart remarks
  • Major · 2-QA to 3-IC Major geometry severity. 312 real geometry edits detected, 28.5% of features. Detailed review recommended.
  • Change · 4-IC to 5-Final Feature count change of +14% detected in CableLine. Possible splits or additions.
  • Note · Pipeline-wide StructurePoint drives 31% of all attribute changes, the busiest layer across all steps.

Geometry severity classification

Every layer comparison is assigned a severity band from the percentage of features with real spatial displacement.

  • None 0%
  • Stable under 2%
  • Light 2 to 10%
  • Moderate 10 to 25%
  • Major over 25%

Context

Developed during my work at Sharper Shape to address a real gap in our GIS pipeline QA process. Geospatial datasets pass through multiple processing steps (digitisation, QA review, independent check, final delivery), and tracking what actually changed between steps was previously a manual, time-consuming task.

GeoQC Flow automates that process entirely. It handles heterogeneous layer structures, variable ID field naming conventions, and mixed geometry types within the same pipeline run. The HTML output replicates Sharper Shape's internal design system, so reports are immediately familiar to the team.
